I’ve been an adult for all of it; I’ve had a front row seat for two decades of moral panics, parental freakouts, and bizarre political theater. articles.summary: Update, November 19: Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle has announced that the detonation will be postponed until November 23. On Friday, the US Army is scheduled to detonate roughly 11,000 pounds of lead azide, an unstable bomb-making chemical, in southeastern Iowa. The explosion will send a plume of lead-contaminated dust across a hundred-mile swath of the Midwest. Though the Army reportedly knew of the potential hazard for years, residents of the 400-person community of Middletown, who will be expected to evacuate, were given just a month’s notice of the plan to ignite 68 barrels of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. But the dust plume’s potential 100-mile path extends far beyond Middletown, and the other communities in its path — as well as Iowa’s governor —only became aware of the plan on Monday, after the Army made a public announcement, according to the Washington Sun . The Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club’s Iowa chapter filed a lawsuit on Thursday to halt the detonation. Army representatives told Middletown residents that the 40-year-old explosive stockpile must be detonated now because it has degraded to the point of becoming unstable to move.
